clue.text: Oxford difficult to get into? This may help

definitions.text: Oxford difficult to get into? This may help

parts.words: Oxford difficult to get into? This may help
parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced shoe, not the university, and a tight one needs a tool to ease the heel in

explanation.surface: An applicant wonders what might help them win a place at the hard-to-enter university.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Oxford University and admissions; the Oxford is really a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved implement slipped behind the heel helps a foot slide into a tight shoe.

clue.text: Pressure beginning to split lock

indicators.note: the beginning of the word split means only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Strain builds as someone starts to pick apart a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is force or strain applied, the same idea as pressure.

clue.text: Band of gold artist fixed around box

indicators.note: the gold and artist pieces are fixed around the outside of the box piece, enclosing it

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A ring band made of gold by an artist is set around a jewellery box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed around' turns the gold and artist pair into a two-part shell; 'Band' is the musical sense, not a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of musicians, especially a large classical ensemble, is an orchestra.

clue.text: Listen to all the Commandments being read out and cheer

parts.note: to listen to is to hear
there are ten Commandments in all

explanation.surface: A congregation is heartened by hearing the Commandments read aloud in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to encourage or hearten them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Use force to, remove magistrate from hearing

indicators.note: from hearing means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a reeve was a local magistrate or official in medieval England

explanation.surface: A magistrate is forcibly ejected from a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reave is an archaic verb for plundering, carrying off by force.

clue.text: Poor firm subsequently in profit

parts.note: firm means hard, as of a surface
to be up is to be ahead, in profit

explanation.surface: A business is short of cash, though later it shows a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money, impoverished, is an idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: It may be the thing required

definitions.meaning: grammatically, the word 'the' is the definite one of its kind in the parts of speech

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite one; separately an item or object is called an article.

clue.text: Condescend to be proclaimed as a native of Europe

indicators.note: proclaimed means spoken out loud, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: a Dane is a native of Denmark in Europe

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to being announced as a European.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something beneath one's dignity, which is to condescend.

clue.text: Introduces hospital dept with journalists gathered round

indicators.note: the journalists gather round the hospital department, enclosing it

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Reporters cluster round a hospital department as someone introduces it.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone is to introduce them formally.

clue.text: An instinctive set of impulses keeps companion lively

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the id in Freudian theory is the instinctive part of the psyche
a mate is a companion

explanation.surface: A psychological description of instinct keeping someone in good company and spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated describes someone full of life and spirit, a synonym.

clue.text: Competition that the enemy threatens to win?

definitions.text: Competition that the enemy threatens to win?

parts.words: Competition that the enemy threatens to win?
parts.note: time is the old enemy, so a contest where the clock may beat you is meant

explanation.surface: A contest the opposing side looks set to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is the proverbial phrase for time, not a military foe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush to finish something before a deadline is a contest with the clock.

clue.text: The woman without warmth found cover

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the woman's word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: she is a woman
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A woman feeling the cold found something to cover herself with.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to cover it with its scabbard.

clue.text: Enemy act almost destroyed old city

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order
almost means the word act is not quite complete, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A hostile act all but wiped out an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter from ACT to give AC; ENEMY plus AC is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mycenae was a Bronze Age Greek city, the seat of Agamemnon.

clue.text: Be proud, and put up with striking

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
workers out are on strike

explanation.surface: A worker is proud yet tolerant during industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proud' means sticking out, as a surface standing above its surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proud projects beyond the surface around it, so it protrudes.

clue.text: Traditionalists who may recall what railways used to be like

definitions.text: who may recall what railways used to be like
definitions.meaning: a former train conductor, an aged railwayman, remembers the past

explanation.definitionFit: Conservative members of a group resisting change are its long-serving core; also an elderly railway conductor.

clue.text: Regular time for episode

parts.note: even means regular, as of a steady pace

explanation.surface: A recurring time slot for an instalment of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or occurrence, a synonym.

clue.text: Layers of superficial matter from English essayist hiding essential element

indicators.note: hiding means one piece covers another inside it

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
the pith is the essential part or core

explanation.surface: An English writer conceals the heart of the matter beneath surface layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' makes the English essayist's pieces a shell; Elia was Charles Lamb's pen name, a standard crossword essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Epithelial tissue forms the outer covering layers of the body and its organs.

clue.text: Leaks? Have a word with servants

parts.note: to see someone is to meet and talk with them
pages are young servants

explanation.surface: A household suspects leaks and wants a word with the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepages are slow escapes of liquid through openings, a form of leak.

clue.text: An astronomical time taken 'by English coming to agreement

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A treaty signed by England is timed by the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray mark before 'by' is an OCR blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the moon's age at the start of the year, used for calendar reckoning.

clue.text: Army uprising in that place where they're in action?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: An army revolt breaks out where soldiers are fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns the Army piece in a down clue; the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the region where military operations take place.

clue.text: Was in role in charge, like a school-teacher?

parts.note: to have played a part is to have acted

explanation.surface: Someone who took a part and was in command, as a teacher would.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means instructive, inclined to teach or lecture.

clue.text: Restrict prisoner? Good!

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
fine is an exclamation of approval meaning good

explanation.surface: Someone welcomes locking up a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to keep within limits, restrict.

clue.text: A male in employment, happily occupied

parts.note: used means employed, put to use

explanation.surface: A man who is employed is contentedly busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained or kept pleasantly busy is to be amused.

clue.text: Plain dish with gold on edge

indicators.note: on edge means the gold sits at the end, after the dish

parts.note: a plate is a dish
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A simple dish with a gold rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high flat land, a raised plain.

clue.text: A hindrance crossing river brings alarm

indicators.note: crossing means one piece spans another, holding it inside

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: An obstacle across a river triggers a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, an alarm.

clue.text: Dishonest actor appearing as a philosopher

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked, dishonest
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: A crooked performer passes himself off as a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham was the English utilitarian philosopher.

clue.text: One who crooned Love is a Game

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A singer's song title claims love is a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game of chance played on cards.

clue.text: Islands all granite with trees looking gnarled

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An island landscape of granite and twisted trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greater Antilles are the large Caribbean islands such as Cuba and Jamaica.

clue.text: Dog traversing Somerset terrain

indicators.note: traversing means the word runs across the boundary between the two clue words

explanation.surface: A dog crosses the Somerset countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county in the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Dash into shallow water in the Cape

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a ford is a shallow crossing of a river
elan is dash, flair

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into shallow water at the Cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreland is a promontory or headland, which is what a cape is.
